title: Muse Spark 1.3 Made a Game So Fun I Couldn't Stop Developing It
author: Bastion80
selftext:
I wanted to test Muse Spark and gave it a prompt to make this game. For a free model (free on OpenCode), I was really happy with the outcome, and the game was somewhat fun, even if it was just a test. This was the first version Muse gave me: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NO7HWddAnhs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NO7HWddAnhs)

After 2 days of fixing bugs and adding features using Muse, this was the result: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYUL-kPpITw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYUL-kPpITw)

After this, I switched to Codex, using mostly SOL High and Astra Medium, with me as a human orchestrator. The result is what you see in the video.

Rhythm-based gameplay, procedurally generated levels, 183 weapons, 247 powerups, editor/creator/generator for weapons/powerups/level styles/enemies, custom music (MP3) support, leaderboard, many game modes, controller support with aim assist. The gameplay is on a old GTX 970 (including OBS recording, which is eating FPS in the video, still 50 FPS). HTML with JavaScript timers for beat sync (less accurate) and EXE with a precise beat sync server.

I have so much fun playing it that I wanted to share it with you. Everything is AI-generated (including assets and music, except the menu music).

Sharing because now it's fun, without any game-breaking bugs, and just how I like it.
